pathway.title: Ford Otosan · historical funding review
pathway.question: What does the April 2024 published funding plan support, and which access and cash-use assumptions change its coverage?

cells.text: The source's 2024 plan starts January 1, 2024; it is not twelve new months from our April review date. In TRY billions, sources are cash 15.2 + cash FFO 63 + planned bond proceeds 16 + capex-facility availability 15 = 109.2. Uses are short maturities 33.8 + working capital 8.6 + additional WC swings 2 + unstressed reported capex 46.3 = 90.7. This reconstructs approximately 1.2x using the displayed rounded components, not the agency's undisclosed full working model.

tabs.label: Conditions on the dividend and capex cases

cells.text: These are separately stipulated cases. The source's stress assessment excludes committed dividends, while its unstressed plan has distributions. The overlay exposes why those cash-use assumptions matter; it does not prove a real shortfall or that all facility funds can finance dividends. The capex reduction is a stated illustrative use of the source's mitigation estimate, not its reported 1.2x case.

tabs.label: Calculation scope and separate currency scales

cells.text: Two source totals, six ratios and six balances were independently checked using Fractions/integer rounding; two missingness controls preserve gaps rather than zero. The helper stores four-decimal ratios; source amounts remain approximate. Currency units are TRY billions here versus TRY millions in the financial table; no new FX conversion was applied. No source amount or residual was overwritten.

CP-2H changes how the funding case is used: preliminary/expected ratings do not establish completed bond proceeds. The agency's liquidity assessment assumes bond placement; it also identifies a signed capex facility, whose permitted uses and drawability still matter. Treating both as unrestricted settled cash would overstate demonstrated access. Conversely, a conditional removal of funds is a stress test, not evidence that financing actually failed.

Do not substitute the adjusted forecast table's FFO for the liquidity narrative's cash-FFO input, or use Fitch's adjusted available cash in place of the S&P balance. Likewise, S&P gross leverage cannot establish Fitch net-leverage headroom. The agency divergence carries methodology/condition information, not a financing guarantee or mechanically cheaper market price.

The causal risk is operating/currency or cash-access weakness during investment and distributions → less usable funding → more dependence on execution and cash-use flexibility. The contrary case is completed ordinary-course funding, protected operating generation and feasible spending/distribution adjustment. Verify final documents/actions, actual access and cash uses before deciding which case applies. No realised failure, default or LME intent is inferred.

tabs.label: Unassessed legal capacity, feasibility and outcomes

cells.text: No complete executed maturity/credit/indenture/intercreditor package, facility certificate, binding final bond terms, market quotes or current access/outcomes. Exact legal capacity, full funding need, refinancing feasibility, creditor priority/recovery and LME vulnerability score remain unassessed. This is genuine downstream use of CP-2H within scope, not full CP-3C coverage.

CP-4 needs operative documents for capacity/priority. CP-5/CP-5A should audit the provisional ratings, unmatched definitions, conditional liquidity assumptions and retained source-display residuals. CP-6 receives the source-based case and countercase. Delivery may reproduce these checked handoffs with date, issuer, conditions and units; actual deliverables replace CP-MEMO.
